response: AmazonHistoryPrice reports that Phi-2, as a buyer, had a weak baseline (13.64% deal rate, -1.58 SNP), but with OG-Narrator its performance rose sharply to 88.08% deal rate and 2015.98 SNP; the paper also says OG-Narrator raised buyer deal rates from 26.67% to 88.88% and produced roughly a tenfold profit increase, even for a model that had not been aligned. In EAI, OpenChat-7b is described as having notably high acceptance rates in bargaining/ultimatum settings, indicating greater willingness to cooperate/accept lower offers, whereas strongly RLHF-aligned LLaMA-2 70B showed markedly lower acceptance rates and a stricter threshold for acceptance. So the contrast is that OG-Narrator dramatically boosts an unaligned model’s bargaining success, while OpenChat-7b already exhibits more cooperative acceptance behavior than RLHF-aligned LLaMA-2.
judge_justification: The response correctly compares the two papers’ key finding: an unaligned model (Phi-2) performs poorly at baseline but improves dramatically with OG-Narrator in AmazonHistoryPrice, while OpenChat-7b in EAI shows unusually high cooperation/acceptance relative to strongly RLHF-aligned models like LLaMA-2. It captures the main synthesis that non-RLHF-aligned models can be more cooperative, though under different experimental conditions, and includes relevant quantitative detail without introducing major errors.
